title: Analog scaling: from raw counts to a percentage
summary: Scale a raw count from 0 to 1000 into a percentage with integer arithmetic, and raise a warning at 50 percent and an alarm at 80 percent.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show the accuracy, noise or calibration of a real analog input.
objectives: Scale a raw count to engineering units with whole numbers, without losing the part of the value below the divisor.
See that integer division drops the remainder, and choose an integer type wide enough for the intermediate product.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: The scenario inputs are BOOL, so this lesson does not read a real analog input: src/Scaling.st counts Raw up by 100 on each scan while Enable is TRUE, as a stand-in for a signal that rises from 0 to 1000. Write the scaling: Percent is Raw scaled from 0..1000 to 0..100.
stages.checkpoint: Percent is the right percentage of Raw at every step, Warn turns ON at 50 percent and Alarm at 80 percent.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Enable rises at {{t:10}} ms and Raw is 100 after that scan. Predict Warn and Alarm at {{t:40}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:80}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:Scaling.Warn=false,Scaling.Alarm=false@40|Both OFF}} at {{t:40}} ms; {{v:Scaling.Warn=true,Scaling.Alarm=false@50|only Warn}} at {{t:50}} ms; {{v:Scaling.Warn=true,Scaling.Alarm=true@80|both ON}} at {{t:80}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starter keeps Percent at 0 until Raw reaches 1000, so Warn and Alarm stay OFF while Raw rises and turn ON together at full scale. Change the scaling so that Percent is the right percentage of Raw at every step, not only at full scale. Leave the stand-in for Raw and the two comparisons as they are.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named Scaling and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:40}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:80}} ms: Warn rises at {{t:50}} ms when Raw is 500, and Alarm at {{t:80}} ms when Raw is 800.
stages.checkpoint: Each output rises once; Alarm is never ON while Warn is OFF; Enable falling at {{t:110}} ms clears both.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Why is DINT used here? Which values does the program form on its way to Percent, and would each of them fit in a 16-bit INT? What would adding half the divisor before the division change, and for which values of Raw?
stages.checkpoint: You can list the values the program forms on its way to Percent and say which of them needs more than 16 bits. The scenario checks the two thresholds only; it does not check the rounding of other values.

hints.text: Look at the line that writes Percent and work it out by hand for Raw = 500, with whole numbers only: an integer division drops the remainder, so 500 / 1000 is 0.
Percent := (Raw * 100) / 1000; keeps the full product before dividing. Leave Raw and the two comparisons as they are.

faultCases: The starter keeps Percent at 0 until Raw reaches 1000, so Warn and Alarm stay OFF while Raw rises and turn ON together at full scale.
